contradicting_evidence: The Devil's Advocate's strongest points are (1) the single POST to a /graphql endpoint on a state-affiliated .gov.cn host, bracketed by GETs in a ~3-second window (events 8119109, 8119110, 8119111), which is the only non-GET in scope and independently drove both ml.autoencoder on src_ip ip_fba063c6ce6c (burstiness feature exceeded) and ml.mahalanobis on the user; and (2) bobadiah's persistent re-attempts to blocked heart.org across four separate days (events 8119359-8119361, 8120682, 8120814, 8120815), since retrying a blocked destination is a documented C2 fallback pattern. These do not change the disposition: the POST is a single 995-byte request with no repetition, no periodicity, and no second POST anywhere in the 11-day span, which is how ordinary web pages submit search/telemetry; and every heart.org attempt returned an identical 1180-byte HTTP 403 block page with zero successful retrieval and no path variation, consistent with a human or a stale tab/bookmark re-hitting a categorised-blocked health site. Combined with the absent baselines (n_baseline_windows=0, null z) and mad=0 burst signals on counts of 3 and 1, there is no corroborated malicious channel. The /graphql POST is worth a closeout check if it ever repeats.

summary: Both the Investigator and the Devil's Advocate independently converge on a false-positive reading. The retrieved events show a small number of ordinary GET/HEAD browser requests by two users (cabshier / u_3009bf59c3ab and bobadiah / u_f6c05600d84d) to well-known public sites (dailymail.co.uk, whatsapp.com, mofa.go.jp, miit.gov.cn, heart.org, hubspot.com, startribune.com, airbnb.com) with browser-typical byte volumes, standard Chrome user agents, no beaconing cadence, and no successful access to blocked content. The critical fused score (0.99) is a stacking artefact of ~51 low-confidence detectors firing on entities with essentially no baseline history: burst signals report z_is_infinite with mad=0 on counts of 3 and 1, and the user's own bytes_out/event_count baselines return n_baseline_windows=0 with null z. The high graph degree on miit.gov.cn is explained by five unrelated corporate principals browsing the same public government website. Two residual oddities — a single 995-byte /graphql POST in bobadiah's miit.gov.cn window and repeated blocked heart.org attempts across four days — are individually suspicious in shape but lack the repetition, periodicity, or any successful retrieval that a real C2 or exfiltration channel would exhibit. Disposition: false positive; recommend detector hygiene and a web-category/user-education note rather than IR action.
